messages.subject: rstan: x-axis in traceplot
parts:
I ran
sflist <- mclapply(1:3, function(i) stan(fit=rb, data=stanDat, iter=4000, chains=1,
seed=seed, chain_id=i, refresh=-1,
warmup=500, thin=2,
control=list(adapt_delta=0.99, max_treedepth=13)),
mc.cores=3)
a10 <- sflist2stanfit(sflist)
myfit <- a10

After which
> x <- extract(myfit, "lp__", permuted=FALSE, inc_warmup=TRUE)
> dim(x)
[1] 2000 3 1
> traceplot(myfit, pars=c("beta[1]", "beta[2]", "theta[1]", "theta[2]", "lp__", "sigma_alpha", "sigma_gamma", "sigma_beta", "gamma_share", "sigma_total"), window=400, ask=TRUE)

The traceplots show an x access extending up to 4,000, not 2,000.
The gray warmup area extends to 500.

Since there are only 2,000 points in each chain, I found this a bit
suprising. OTOH, the window I specified was meant (by me) to be 400 of
the original (rather than recorded) iterations, and it was interpreted
consistent with that.

If I could magnify the graph would there be gaps at every other point?

This is with development code from a little beyond stan 2.01.

BTW, despite the extreme control values, the results stank, with
*median* effective sample size of 1.9. From the traceplots it looks as
if 2 of the 3 chains were completely stuck. 1 of the chains ran much
longer the others (~ 16 hours vs 3 hours).

I guess I should try pushing for even smaller steps. This is
structurally the same model for counts that had problems a few days ago,
for which the solution was high adapt_delta and treedepth to match.

Ross Boylan

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] rstan: x-axis in traceplot
parts:
The x-axis indicates the iteration number of the sampling process and I think it is right in your case as you specified 500 for warmup and 4000 for the total number of iterations.  The draws are thinned does not mean the iterations of sampling does not happen. 

--
Jiqiang
